links.outcome: Precision of LLM-generated medication-indication pairs on clinician review of a random sample
links.effect: 418 of 465 sampled pairs judged correct (precision 89.9%), so about 10% were incorrect; external NHANES agreement 84% (210/250).
links.quote: A random subset of 465 medication-indication pairs was selected for clinical validation, of which 418 were assessed to be correct (a precision of 89.9%).

unlisted_practices: Using LLM-generated confidence score thresholds (0.75) to trade off error rate against knowledge base size
External validation of LLM-generated knowledge against participant-reported survey data (NHANES)

screen.reason: The study develops a pipeline using GPT-4 and MedCAT to extract medication-indication pairs and explicitly investigates the use of LLM confidence score thresholding to optimize the error rate and knowledge base quality, validated by clinicians.

primary.practice: confidence score thresholding and clinical expert validation
